source: Request contract between the local connector (host/services.py) and our service: the client builds requests and checks replies against this file, and the server accepts requests by it

x-transport.endpoint: Endpoint in the client config: https://<IPv4>:<port> (direct over a private network, the server's own certificate) or https://<hostname>[:<port>] (a TLS-terminating tunnel such as Cloudflare Tunnel)
x-transport.trust: IPv4 endpoint: trust only the certificate SHA-256 fingerprint pinned in the client config (pin kind cert_sha256), not the system trust store. Hostname endpoint: the system trust store plus the hostname check (pin kind ca), and both server_keys and e2e_keys are required, so a TLS-terminating edge can neither forge an answer nor read a credential or served content. Never fall back to plaintext: with e2e_keys set, a request that cannot be sealed is not sent
x-transport.response_signature: With server_keys in the client config, every answer must carry X-Agent-Server-Signature: v=1; kid=<16 hex: sha256(raw public key)[:16]>; ts=<unix seconds>; sig=<base64 Ed25519 signature> over the UTF-8 lines agent-svc-response/1, status, METHOD, path without query, the request's X-Agent-Challenge (32 hex, fresh per request), ts, sha256 hex of the body bytes, joined by a newline. The client refuses an answer that is unsigned, signed by a key not in server_keys, bound to another request (replay) or more than 300 seconds off its clock, never uses it, and closes the shell gate (reason unverified); an unsigned 5xx, 403 or 429 (the tunnel edge's own page) counts as an unreachable server and is backed off (an unsigned Retry-After is honored up to 60 seconds); with e2e_keys, a signed success that is not a sealed answer, or one that does not open, is never used either. Verifier: host/services.py _verify_response
x-transport.egress: Only the local connector process (host/services.py) sends; sessions, hooks, plugins and the UI never connect to the service directly
x-transport.e2e: End-to-end envelope (host/e2e.py, both sides), used for every request but GET /health whenever the client config has e2e_keys (required for a hostname endpoint, optional for the IPv4 one). The client makes a fresh X25519 key per request; shared = X25519(that key, the first key in e2e_keys); HKDF-SHA256(shared, salt agent-svc-e2e/1, info "keys" + ephemeral public key + server public key) gives 64 bytes: the request key (first 32) and the answer key (last 32). Outer request: POST to an outer path (x-transport outer_paths) with X-Agent-E2E: v=1; kid=<16 hex: sha256(raw X25519 public key)[:16]>; epk=<base64 ephemeral public key>; ts=<unix seconds>, X-Agent-Challenge and Content-Type application/octet-stream; body = 12-byte nonce || AES-256-GCM(request key, inner, aad). Inner: compact JSON {method, path (with query), headers} + newline + the raw body; the headers are the credential headers (Authorization, X-Agent-Account, X-Agent-Device, X-Agent-Claude, X-Agent-Timestamp, X-Agent-Nonce, X-Agent-Signature) and Content-Type, which never travel outside the envelope. AAD: the lines agent-svc-e2e/1, req (or resp), POST, the outer path, kid, epk, ts, challenge. Answer: 200 application/octet-stream, body = random 12-byte nonce || AES-256-GCM(answer key, compact JSON {status, headers} + newline + body, aad with resp); errors found before the envelope opens (limits, bad_envelope) are plain JSON. The server refuses a timestamp more than 300 seconds off, an unknown kid (before any key work), an envelope that does not open, a login route outside the login outer path, and a replayed ephemeral key, all as 400 bad_envelope counted as a failed authentication of the client IP. The Ed25519 response signature covers the outer answer (the ciphertext), so a client checks it before decrypting and a signature never confirms a guess about the plaintext

outer_paths.POST /svc/v1/x: every sealed route except the two login routes
outer_paths.POST /svc/v1/auth/login/x: sealed login start and finish (keeps the edge's per-IP login rate rule)
outer_paths.GET /health: plain; carries no credential or private content

x-auth.note: One service key per client (we issue it); stored at <data dir>/secrets/services.key, readable by the current user only; never in logs, events, the outbox or error text; unrelated to Claude credentials

x-headers.name: X-Agent-Challenge
x-headers.value: 32 random lowercase hex per request, sent only when the client config has server_keys; the server signs its answer over it (x-transport response_signature)

x-headers.name: X-Agent-E2E
x-headers.value: v=1; kid=<16 hex>; epk=<base64 32-byte X25519 public key>; ts=<unix seconds>, sent only when the client config has e2e_keys (x-transport e2e); the credential headers then travel inside the envelope only

x-validation: Both ends validate against the request schema: the client builds the body only from the schema and drops fields the schema does not have before sending; the server answers 422 bad_request on extra fields or a wrong type or length; cross-field limits (x-limits) are checked on both ends

x-client-config.path: <data dir>/services/client.json (absent: the shipped host/client_defaults.json; written by `agent_core.py connect`, from what the operator gives: endpoint, server keys and e2e keys; agent-svc-vps admin server-key prints them)

sha256.description: two fingerprints: the old and the new certificate are both accepted during rotation

server_keys.description: the server's Ed25519 public keys (raw 32 bytes, base64) that sign every answer; two only while the server rotates its key

e2e_keys.description: the server's X25519 public keys (raw 32 bytes, base64) that requests are sealed to (x-transport e2e; the first is used); two only while the server rotates its key; needs server_keys

anyOf.description: direct: the server's own self-signed certificate is pinned; server_keys optional; e2e_keys optional (needs server_keys)

sha256.description: two fingerprints: the old and the new certificate are both accepted during rotation

server_keys.description: the server's Ed25519 public keys (raw 32 bytes, base64) that sign every answer; two only while the server rotates its key

e2e_keys.description: the server's X25519 public keys (raw 32 bytes, base64) that requests are sealed to (x-transport e2e; the first is used); two only while the server rotates its key; needs server_keys

anyOf.description: tunnel: system trust store and hostname check, every answer signed by one of server_keys and every request but GET /health sealed to e2e_keys (no plaintext fallback)

server_keys.description: the server's Ed25519 public keys (raw 32 bytes, base64) that sign every answer; two only while the server rotates its key

e2e_keys.description: the server's X25519 public keys (raw 32 bytes, base64) that requests are sealed to (x-transport e2e; the first is used); two only while the server rotates its key; needs server_keys

x-outbox.note: one line per request, including previews that are never sent (preview=true, status=null); body_text is the exact bytes of the request body that was sent (UTF-8), without the Authorization header

SessionRef.description: random id generated for each session on this machine; not a session name, project name or path

SessionKind.description: auto = a session that advances on its own; direct = a session the user works in directly

ServedRole.description: control = scheduling session; auto = a session that advances on its own; plugin = plugin

Savings.description: savings computed by the server from the uploaded counts; amounts to 6 decimal places, pct to 4; usd and tokens may be negative (compaction can cost more than it saves)

DiagEstimateRequest.description: One-time summary for the free usage diagnostic: counts and amounts only, with no session or project hashes, per-day rows, paths, names or text. The server also checks that fields agree with each other, outside the schema; if they do not, it answers 422 bad_request. When there is too little data to estimate, it answers 422 too_little_data

by_model.description: one row per model (past 40 models, the rest are merged into other); main conversation and subagents kept separate

dispatches.description: counted by the first word of the subagent description (a word from the public tools.diagnostic.TYPE_WORDS, or other); no other text is sent

by_responses.description: sessions bucketed by reply count (item k = number of sessions with [2^k, 2^(k+1)) replies; the last item includes everything above)

DiagEstimate.description: Estimated monthly savings (numbers and dates only): dollars and hours for each item, with lower and upper bounds; pct = total as a share of spending; reference = the savings rate we measured ourselves

preview.description: true = only builds the request body so the customer can see it; nothing is sent

body_text.description: the exact request body that was sent; null for GET/DELETE

status.description: null when previewing or when the connection fails

error.description: local errors such as a failed connection or a timeout; never contains the key

x-inventory.purpose: connectivity and key check ('Test connection' on the settings page)
x-inventory.retention: no content stored; access log (client_id, time, status code) kept 30 days

x-inventory.purpose: check whether a new update package exists; sends no project, session or content
x-inventory.default: on (only shows a notice when a new version exists)
x-inventory.retention: download record (client_id, version, time) kept 90 days

routes.x-response-body: raw: tar package containing manifest.json and manifest.sig (Ed25519); the client verifies the signature with the pinned public key

x-inventory.purpose: download the update package; sends only the target and version in the path
x-inventory.retention: download record (client_id, version, time) kept 90 days

pinned_version.description: the version this session is bound to; otherwise the version the client pinned for this role; otherwise null (= the current version on the channel)

channel.description: the channel this served version is on now

pinned.description: the request carried a pinned version

catalog.description: the catalog line for this phase; an empty string when there is none

x-inventory.purpose: fetch the content the service serves for each phase; sends only the random session id, role, phase, pinned version and channel
x-inventory.retention: request content not stored; access log kept 30 days

x-inventory.purpose: sends only the random session id and role; receives this session's parameters in return
x-inventory.default: on (once when the session opens; not sent when served content is turned off)

error_template.description: first line of the error after templating (host/incident.py template: paths, URLs, quoted strings, numbers and identifiers are replaced with placeholders); the raw error line is never sent

error_sha256.description: sha256 of the redacted first line (used only to count how many distinct errors there are)

file_ext.description: extension of the file involved; no path or file name

x-inventory.purpose: incident reports, fed to the lesson-curation pipeline (no code, file contents or paths)
x-inventory.retention: kept until a lesson is made or rejected from it, for at most 180 days; session_ref is not stored

request.description: The server also checks that fields agree with each other, outside the schema; if they do not, it answers 422 bad_request. If day is not a calendar date or is outside the date range the server accepts, it answers 422 bad_day

task_type.description: first word of the subagent description (the routing task type)

project_hash.description: HMAC(local salt, project); can group but cannot recover the project name

success.description: null = not recorded (session records do not keep results)

savings.description: raw counts the savings formula needs; omit when absent. The server computes amounts; the client does not

route.description: routed subagent turns, one row per (model, long) per day

long.description: this turn's prompt is over long_prompt.over in the public price list for this model

index.description: segmented reads of index files, one row per (model, file_tokens) per day

file_tokens.description: token estimate for the whole file that was read

compact.description: checkpoint compactions, one row per ref per day; steps that cross a day boundary are joined on the server by ref

ref.description: random id generated for each compaction, not the session id

start.description: the compaction day's starting point; null when the starting point is not on this day

steps.description: each later main-conversation request as [context, index into models]

x-inventory.purpose: one usage summary per day (numbers and hashes only); in return: cross-customer reports, savings amounts computed by the server, and tuning advice
x-inventory.default: off (the customer turns it on; the exact JSON is shown before the first upload)
x-inventory.retention: 13 months; deleted within 30 days of being turned off, or immediately from the settings page (DELETE /metrics)

x-inventory.purpose: immediately delete all of this customer's usage summaries on the server
x-inventory.default: sent only when the customer clicks delete
x-inventory.retention: no content stored; deletion record (client_id, time, row count) kept 13 months

values.description: template parameters: numbers, or strings from a fixed set (dates, model ids, savings item names)

x-inventory.purpose: fetch the cross-customer reports; sends no content
x-inventory.default: available at any time (existing reports can still be fetched after usage upload is turned off)
x-inventory.retention: no content stored; access log kept 30 days

x-inventory.purpose: saved amounts computed on the server from the uploaded counters
x-inventory.default: only while the metrics upload is on

on.description: false = stop the weekly savings email; true = send it again

x-inventory.purpose: turn the weekly savings email on or off
x-inventory.default: off; sent only when the customer turns the weekly savings email off or back on (the email itself is on by default for customers who turned the usage upload on)
x-inventory.retention: the setting and the time it changed, kept while the account exists; audit record 13 months

x-inventory.purpose: one-time usage aggregate for the free diagnostic; the server answers an estimated monthly saving (numbers only)
x-inventory.default: off; sent once, only after the exact body was shown and `--consent` given
x-inventory.retention: body not stored; a per-account count per UTC day kept 30 days; access log 30 days

type_word.description: first word of the subagent description, split on whitespace; the rest of the text is not sent

dispatch_no.description: which subagent dispatch this is in the session

project_hash.description: HMAC(local salt, project); can group but cannot recover the project name

brief_rule.description: the speed-up rule the calling agent forwards unchanged into the subagent brief

brief_forward.description: the instruction to forward brief_rule into the subagent brief

x-inventory.purpose: asks which model and effort to use before a subagent dispatch (sends only the first word of the task type and a count, not the description text)
x-inventory.default: on (on by default while Services is on)
x-inventory.retention: counts per decision per day; request bodies not stored

x-inventory.purpose: asks whether now is a good time to compact the context (sends only counters)
x-inventory.default: on (on by default while Services is on)
x-inventory.retention: counts per decision per day; request bodies not stored

head.description: first word of the command (if it is in the public list of common commands, otherwise other); arguments and paths are not sent

x-inventory.purpose: bounded runs (boundrun) ask how long this command may go without output before it stops, and what its total time limit is
x-inventory.default: on (on by default while Services is on)
x-inventory.retention: counts per decision per day; request bodies not stored

x-inventory.purpose: read-only token for plugin updates (expires after 1 hour); sends only the client version
x-inventory.retention: sha256 of the token, account, device, time and expiry, kept 30 days; the token itself is not stored
